entries.appliesTo: operators providing AI companions to users in the state

dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 6-63-2(a) — 'It shall be unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless such AI companion contains a protocol for addressing: (1) Possible suicidal ideation or self-harm expressed by a user'
dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 6-63-3 — 'An operator shall provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction'
dutySources.incident-reporting: § 6-63-2(b) — 'operators shall file annual reports with the office of the attorney general which shall include the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics'

sources.scope: § 6-63-1(1)(i) — '"AI companion" means a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user'
sources.ageFocus: § 6-63-1(8) — '"User" means any person who uses an AI companion within the state'
sources.aiDisclosure: § 6-63-3 — 'notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction'
sources.crisisProtocol: § 6-63-2(a) — 'a notification shall be provided to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected'
sources.penaltyMax: § 6-63-4(b) — 'civil penalties up to fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) per day'
sources.enforcer: § 6-63-4(a) — 'The attorney general shall be empowered to enforce this chapter, including the power to investigate, sue, and seek injunctions'

flags: aiDisclosure coded session-start is lossy: § 6-63-3 also requires the not-a-human notification 'at least every three (3) hours for continuing AI companion interactions'
annual AG reporting duty begins July 1, 2027 (§ 6-63-2(b)); act effective January 1, 2027 (SECTION 2)
penalty proceeds earmarked: 'fines directed to suicide prevention programs' (§ 6-63-4(b))
crisis protocol also covers 'Possible physical harm to others expressed by a user' (§ 6-63-2(a)(2)), beyond self-harm
